page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i3.13xlarge is a storage-intensive and memory-dense server instance running on KVM hypervisor technology. Powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, the instance delivers 52 dedicated vCPUs alongside 384.0 GB of system memory, yielding a ratio of 7.38 GB per vCPU. It features direct-attached local storage capacity comprising 11,519 GB of SSD storage and provides a baseline network throughput of 16 Gbps.

The hardware configuration prioritizes local storage capacity and substantial memory allocation per compute thread. The inclusion of 11.5 TB of bundled SSD storage eliminates reliance on external network-attached volumes for throughput-sensitive operations, offering high local storage density relative to compute core count. With 384 GB of RAM, the instance accommodates large in-memory working sets alongside persistent local data stores, maximizing resource density within a single virtual server.

Lacking discrete GPU hardware, the ecs.i3.13xlarge is tailored for non-graphic, high-throughput enterprise workloads. Appropriate deployment models include distributed databases, NoSQL datastores, relational databases requiring expansive cache space, big data analytics engines, and intensive ETL pipelines. The local SSD array provides high capacity, though applications requiring multi-region persistence must handle data replication at the software layer.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i3.13xlarge is a storage and memory-dense virtual server instance built on the x86_64 architecture using KVM virtualization. Driven by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz, it provides 52 dedicated vCPUs and 384.0 GB of RAM, resulting in 7.38 GB of memory per core. A key capability of this server is its bundled 11,519 GB local SSD storage array combined with a 16 Gbps baseline network bandwidth profile. This hardware allocation makes the instance suited for input and output intensive applications, high-capacity relational and NoSQL databases, search indexing engines, and large-scale analytical processing jobs that benefit from direct-attached storage density and high memory allocation.
